decision: Port only the LAN Pipes discovery pattern into go_hive as an optional LAN queen-mail federation. Two Hive instances on the same private LAN announce themselves over signed UDP multicast, auto-pair when they share group_id and the group key from group_key_env, and exchange queen mail over HTTPS/JSON. The existing queen mail engine remains the only mail engine: thread sessions, reply watcher, max_depth, daily_limit and mail.jsonl audit are reused. There is no remote session control, no raw prompt path, no second role model and no public/WAN discovery. The schema exposes only five keys; federation, expose, peers, auto_connect, targets and the rest are deliberately absent, not left at defaults.
goal_beyond_request: Let queens on two Hive instances on the same private LAN write to each other with zero peer configuration beyond a shared group id and group key, while preserving local thread sessions, asynchronous replies, mail limits and audit. The peer layer is a transport and admission adapter for queen mail, not a second orchestration model.

feasibility.verdict: 发现和信件传输可移植；远程会话控制不在本设计范围。
feasibility.why: UDP multicast and HTTPS/JSON are standard-library work in Go. The hard part is identity and admission, not the socket: queen mail is already asynchronous and owns thread sessions, reply watchers, depth, daily limits and audit. The peer layer must feed that engine without bypassing participant checks, and a shared group key must not become an internet-wide bearer secret.
reusable_parts: UDP multicast discovery and announce freshness are transport patterns that port to Go without cgo.
HTTPS/JSON request-response, TLS pinning, retries and expiry are standard library work.
Queen mail already has thread sessions, reply delivery, wake-up, max_depth, daily_limit and mail.jsonl audit; the peer layer only supplies remote correspondents and a remote deliverer.
The existing queen mail tools already give queens list_queens and message_queen; remote addresses can be added without a new model tool.
not_portable: The unauthenticated TCP/NDJSON transport and main/sub/master/slave roles from LAN Pipes do not fit Hive.
Raw prompt routing and remote session control would bypass queen/colony runtime, permission boundaries and audit.
Multicast cannot cross the public internet, and a group key is not a public-network identity.
Static peer rosters and manual per-peer tokens are intentionally removed from this design; they are not a fallback.

problem.statement: Queen mail is process-local today: list_queens reads local queens, message_queen delivers into a local thread session, and the reply watcher writes back to a local writer. Two Hive instances on the same LAN have no discovery, no peer identity and no way to address a remote queen without custom HTTP calls.
user_value: A node joins a LAN group with only group_id and a group key env var; existing nodes need no edit.
Remote queens appear automatically as queen_b@hive-office-b@office-lan and are writable with message_queen.
Replies use the existing asynchronous queen mail path: the remote queen answers in her thread session, and the adapter sends the reply back.
The surface stays mail-only: no remote session create/chat/events, no colony or worker control, no new model tool.
The feature is opt-in and disabled by default; when disabled it opens no UDP or TCP socket.
problem.why_not_now: This is an additive Go-only capability for a private LAN, not an upstream Hive feature. It remains design-only until the five-key schema, group auto-pair, the queenmail resolver boundary and a real two-process LAN E2E are accepted.

protocol.name: Hive LAN peer mail
protocol.transport: HTTPS/JSON over TCP for handshake, mail and health; UDP multicast only for discovery
protocol.discovery: Fixed UDP multicast 239.255.71.67:7101; no static peer roster
protocol.auth: Group key admission plus per-node ed25519 identity; TLS certificate pinned
protocol.framing: HTTP JSON request/response; no raw TCP/NDJSON, no WebSocket/SSE
protocol.scope: Same private LAN, flat peer group; queen-initiated mail chains bounded to 4 hops; post-1.0 optional extension

requirements.statement: Keep the feature opt-in and default off: lan_peers.enabled gates all discovery sockets and peer routes; no parity claim, no default model tool and no change to the frozen 1.0 surface.
requirements.acceptance: With lan_peers.enabled false or absent, no UDP socket, TCP listener, peer route or model tool is registered; existing local queen mail tests are unchanged.

requirements.statement: Scope the peer surface to federated queen mail only. Do not add /peer/v1/sessions, remote chat/events/delete, colony or worker control, or a second execution engine.
requirements.acceptance: The only peer routes are handshake, qmail and health; a request for /peer/v1/sessions returns 404; no remote session is created by the feature.

requirements.statement: Discover peers with signed UDP multicast. The announce carries instance identity, endpoint, group id and a group proof, but never a bearer token and never a session.
requirements.acceptance: A forged or stale announce cannot create a peer; a valid group proof and node signature are required; announce data alone never delivers mail.

requirements.statement: Fix group auto-pair: no peers list, no auto_connect key, no targets. Same group_id plus the group key in group_key_env means automatic pairing and connection; a missing key fails closed at startup.
requirements.acceptance: Two nodes with the same group_id and key pair without any peer entry; different group ids or keys do not connect; lan_peers.enabled without the env var fails startup; peers, auto_connect, targets and expose are rejected as unknown keys.

requirements.statement: Generate identity automatically: a stable instance_id and an ed25519 keypair on first run, persisted under HIVE_HOME/lan_peers; pin a peer public key from its signed announce and quarantine a changed key.
requirements.acceptance: No identity key is required in configuration; restarts keep the same instance_id and key; a changed public key is quarantined and does not silently replace the pin.

requirements.statement: Use HTTPS over TCP for handshake, mail and health, with a self-signed certificate pinned from the signed announce. Keep the transport on private LAN addresses only; no raw TCP, no NDJSON and no public/WAN target.
requirements.acceptance: Non-loopback peers require TLS; a public or non-private URL is refused; no letter body is sent over plaintext; no raw TCP or SSE listener is opened.

requirements.statement: Reuse the existing queen mail engine: Mail.Send, Mail.DeliverReply, thread session lookup/creation, reply watcher, max_depth, daily_limit and mail.jsonl audit stay authoritative. Add only a correspondent resolver and a remote deliverer at the edges.
requirements.acceptance: No second mail queue or reply watcher is introduced; local queen mail tests still pass; a remote letter reaches the same thread-session and reply path as a local letter.

requirements.statement: Address remote queens with the three-level form queen_name@peer_node_id@group_id. list_queens merges remote entries from paired peers using the same id, name and title fields as local entries; message_queen accepts the address without a manual target list. Existing claude_code: conversation refs keep their branch; the resolver checks that prefix first.
requirements.acceptance: A paired peer's queens appear with the same id/name/title shape as local entries; a three-part address routes to the remote queen; a one-, two- or four-part address, a group mismatch, or an offline/unknown peer returns a typed error instead of a silent local lookup failure. A claude_code:<queen>:<session> reply still goes to Claude Code, not the remote parser.

requirements.statement: Expose only local queens listed by queen_mail.queens (or all when omitted). Inbound mail is always enabled when lan_peers is enabled; there is no expose, federation or per-peer allowlist key.
requirements.acceptance: A queen outside queen_mail.queens is neither advertised nor writable; an unpaired peer cannot deliver mail; no expose/federation key is accepted.

requirements.statement: Carry a bounded letter envelope: letter_id, trace_id, hops, group_id, from_peer, from_queen, to_peer, to_queen, text, reply_to, ts and signature. Enforce idempotency by letter_id and a fixed max_hops of 4; keep local max_depth independent. Each hop is a queen-initiated message or reply; nothing is forwarded automatically.
requirements.acceptance: A repeated letter_id is delivered once; a chain beyond 4 cross-instance hops is rejected and audited; local max_depth still applies to the local thread. A received letter is not forwarded to a third peer without a queen action.

requirements.statement: Make failures explicit and bounded: offline queue with 24h TTL, retry on 5xx/timeout, no retry on 4xx except 429, per-peer rate limits, and audit rows that identify peer, letter and outcome without logging bodies or secrets.
requirements.acceptance: A peer that disappears mid-send leaves a queued letter that retries or expires with an audit row; duplicates are suppressed; logs and audit contain no group key, token or letter body.

requirements.statement: Verify with fake peers and a real two-process loopback/LAN E2E; a missing real multi-machine run remains an external gap, not PASS. Keep CGO_ENABLED=0 and the generator --check gate.
requirements.acceptance: Fake-peer tests cover discovery, auth, qmail and idempotency; two processes on one host or LAN exchange a letter and a reply; multi-machine is recorded separately; generator --check passes.

non_goals: Do not add remote session create/chat/events/delete or any /peer/v1/sessions route.
Do not expose colony workers, task queues or tool permissions to a peer.
Do not copy the opcteam main/sub/master/slave role model.
Do not support WAN, public discovery, automatic forwarding/relay trees or unbounded multi-hop cascading.
Do not add federation, expose, peers, auto_connect, targets, tls, identity or discovery tuning keys.
Do not add a new default model tool or a colony-specific UI.
Do not reuse HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN as a peer credential.
assumptions: Both peers run hive serve on the same private LAN and can reach each other on a private IPv4 address.
Both peers set the same group_id and provide the same group key through group_key_env.
The LAN forwards UDP multicast 239.255.71.67:7101; if it does not, peer discovery is unavailable in v1.
Each node can generate and persist an instance_id and ed25519 keypair under HIVE_HOME/lan_peers.
Queen mail is already enabled locally; lan_peers only federates it.
A real multi-machine run is required before calling the transport production-ready.

options.name: Signed UDP discovery + HTTPS queen-mail federation over the existing Mail engine
options.reason: Zero peer configuration for a trusted LAN; reuses thread sessions, reply watcher, limits and audit; no second engine; no remote session surface.

options.name: Literal LAN Pipes NDJSON TCP protocol and main/sub/master/slave roles
options.reason: Unauthenticated TCP, raw prompt routing and a second role model; bypasses queen mail and Hive runtime boundaries.

options.name: Remote session control over the existing /api/sessions API
options.reason: Out of scope for this feature: it needs session lifecycle, SSE, permission relay and a target allowlist, which the user explicitly removed.

options.name: Static peer roster with per-peer tokens
options.reason: The user removed peers, tokens and targets; the fixed group_id + group_key pair is the only admission model.

options.name: Extend internal/channels with LAN peers
options.reason: Channels adapt external chat platforms to sessions; they are not a peer discovery or queen-mail admission protocol.

options.name: Direct public HTTPS with mTLS or a VPN/relay
options.reason: Internet support needs a different discovery, NAT and identity model. It is a separate deployment/design, not a lan_peers config switch.

D1.title: Opt-in and mail-only surface
D1.text: lan_peers.enabled gates the UDP discovery socket and the peer routes. When it is false or absent, no socket or route exists. The feature requires queen_mail.enabled; there is no peer session route, no /peer/v1/sessions, no remote chat/events/delete and no colony or worker control.

D2.title: Fixed group discovery
D2.text: Discovery is UDP multicast on 239.255.71.67:7101, TTL 1, announce every 5 seconds and expire after 15 seconds. The announce carries instance_id, name, url, public_key, group_id, capabilities, ts, a group proof and a node signature. There is no peers list, no auto_connect key, no discovery.enabled key and no static fallback; the only discovery configuration is group_id and group_key_env.

D3.title: Identity and group admission
D3.text: On first run, generate an instance_id and an ed25519 keypair under HIVE_HOME/lan_peers. The display name defaults to the hostname; it is not an address key and not a trust source. The announce includes group_proof = HMAC(group_key, instance_id || public_key || ts) and a node signature. A receiver checks group_id, proof, signature and timestamp, then pins the public key. A changed key is quarantined, not silently accepted. If group_key_env is missing while lan_peers.enabled is true, startup fails closed.

D4.title: HTTPS transport
D4.text: Handshake, mail and health use HTTPS over TCP on the peer's advertised private address. The self-signed certificate uses the node's ed25519 identity; the peer pins the public key from the signed announce, not the leaf bytes. Non-loopback peers must use TLS. Bodies are bounded JSON; there is no raw TCP, no NDJSON and no WebSocket/SSE. The peer listener only serves /peer/v1/handshake, /peer/v1/qmail and /peer/v1/health.

D5.title: Connection lifecycle
D5.text: A peer moves through discovered, paired and connected states. A valid announce auto-pairs; a successful handshake connects; a missed announce or health probe marks it offline. A changed IP is accepted only from a signed announce. Group-key rotation requires updating the env var and restarting all nodes; there is no online rotation in v1.

D6.title: Reuse the queen mail engine
D6.text: Mail.Send, Mail.DeliverReply, thread session lookup/creation, reply watcher, max_depth, daily_limit and mail.jsonl audit stay authoritative. The peer layer does not create a second queue, reply watcher or session store. A remote letter enters the same thread-session and reply path as a local letter.

D7.title: Correspondence resolver
D7.text: Add a resolver at the edge of queen mail: local queens come from queen_mail.queens and the queens directory; remote queens come from paired peers and expire with the peer roster. list_queens merges both and returns exactly the existing {id, name, title} shape; a remote id is the full three-level address queen_name@peer_node_id@group_id. The resolver checks ref types in this order: (1) the existing claude_code: prefix via ConversationPrefix/IsConversationRef, which stays unchanged and is handled first; (2) exactly three @-separated segments for a remote queen, with group_id equal to the local discovery.group_id; (3) a local queen id from the roster; (4) a local session or reply ref. ConversationPrefix and QueenIDOfRef are not changed; remote addresses never use that prefix. message_queen parses exactly three @-separated segments: queen_name (the queen id), peer_node_id (the peer's stable instance_id, not its display name) and group_id (must equal the local discovery.group_id). One, two or four segments, an @ inside a segment, or a group mismatch is a typed error. A remote thread's meta records the full writer address so replies route back. Mail.Send target checks and DeliverReply writer checks use the resolver instead of a local-only queens map.

D8.title: Letter envelope and loops
D8.text: The wire letter carries letter_id, trace_id, hops, group_id, from_peer, from_queen, to_peer, to_queen, text, reply_to, ts and signature. letter_id is idempotent for 24 hours. max_hops is fixed at 4 across instances; local max_depth remains independent. A letter beyond max_hops is rejected and audited, never silently delivered. A hop is a deliberate queen message_queen or reply, never automatic forwarding; there is no store-and-forward relay. max_hops only bounds the queen-initiated chain.

D9.title: Exposure and security
D9.text: Only queens listed by queen_mail.queens (or all local queens when omitted) are advertised and writable. The advertised roster carries only the existing id, name and title fields; private profile sections are never exposed. Inbound mail is always enabled when lan_peers is enabled; there is no expose or federation key. The group key is admission only; each node has its own ed25519 identity. Private LAN only, TLS pinned, bounded bodies, per-peer rate limits, and no group key, token or letter body in logs or announce.

D10.title: Package boundary and verification
D10.text: Put discovery, identity, transport and the qmail client/server in internal/lanpeer; keep the server adapter thin; add only a correspondent resolver and remote deliverer interface to internal/queenmail. Do not import internal/server, internal/cli or internal/tools/builtin from internal/lanpeer. No new model tool or UI. Verify with fake peers and a real two-process loopback/LAN E2E; keep CGO_ENABLED=0 and generator --check.

config_contract.authority: Only lan_peers is new; queen_mail.enabled and queen_mail.queens are existing keys. federation, expose, peers, auto_connect, targets, tls, identity and discovery.enabled/group/port/interface are not part of the schema and must be rejected as unknown keys.

fields.name: lan_peers.enabled
fields.meaning: default false; true opens the UDP discovery socket and peer routes; requires queen_mail.enabled and group_key_env

fields.name: lan_peers.discovery.group_id
fields.meaning: non-secret logical group name; announces from another group are ignored and a remote address's third segment must equal it

fields.name: lan_peers.discovery.group_key_env
fields.meaning: environment variable name holding the shared group key; the value is never logged or announced

fields.name: queen_mail.enabled
fields.meaning: existing switch; must be true for local or federated queen mail

fields.name: queen_mail.queens
fields.meaning: local queens that participate and are advertised; omitted means all local queens, empty array means none

config_contract.reload: Read at serve startup; changing enabled, group_id, group_key_env or queen_mail.queens requires a restart in v1.

sequence: Both nodes start with lan_peers.enabled and the same group_id plus group_key_env value; each generates instance_id and ed25519 identity.
Each node sends a signed UDP announce; the receiver verifies group proof, signature and timestamp, then auto-pairs and pins the public key.
The peer client posts /peer/v1/handshake over HTTPS; a challenge-response confirms both node keys and returns the peer queen roster with the same id, name and title fields as local queens.
The ref resolver checks the existing claude_code: prefix first, then the three-level remote address, then a local queen id or session ref.
list_queens merges local and remote entries; the queen writes to queen_b@hive-office-b@office-lan with message_queen.
The sender posts the letter to /peer/v1/qmail; the receiver returns 202 accepted and injects it into the local thread session.
The remote queen answers in her thread session; the reply watcher posts a separate letter back to the writer's /peer/v1/qmail.
A queen may reply to the sender or deliberately write to another peer; each leg increments hops, and nothing is forwarded automatically.
An offline peer queues the letter for up to 24 hours; expiry, duplicate suppression and hop limits are audited.

announce.rule: announce proves group admission and node identity; it carries no bearer token and creates no session

letter_event.response: 202 accepted means the letter entered the local mail path; the queen's reply is a separate POST

ref_kinds.handling: Existing ConversationPrefix / IsConversationRef branch; strip the prefix, split on the last ':' for the queen id; unchanged.
Exactly three @-separated segments; group_id must equal discovery.group_id; resolved before Mail.Send participant checks.
Local roster from queen_mail.queens and the queens directory.

risks.impact: any holder can join the LAN group
risks.mitigation: keep the key in env only, rotate by restarting all nodes, never log or announce it; use a VPN for untrusted networks.
document the limitation; v1 has no static peer fallback; use a VPN/overlay that carries multicast or a separate design.

risks.impact: a member cannot be removed individually
risks.mitigation: rotate the group key; per-node identity prevents impersonation but not admission.
remove its runtime peer record and restart, or rotate the group key; log a clear operator message.

risks.impact: no immediate reply; offline peers delay delivery
risks.mitigation: keep the 24h queue, retry policy and explicit offline/expired errors.

risks.impact: duplicate replies or endless A-B chains
risks.mitigation: letter_id idempotency, trace_id and fixed max_hops=4.

risks.impact: reintroduces targets, SSE, permissions and a second surface
risks.mitigation: mail-only requirement R2, no /peer/v1/sessions, no expose/targets keys.

risks.impact: LAN behavior differs on real networks
risks.mitigation: two-process test is required; record multi-machine as an external gap, not PASS.

open_questions: Group-key rotation is restart-only in v1; is an online rotation endpoint needed later, or is restart acceptable?
A changed node public key is quarantined; should recovery be deleting its runtime peer record, rotating the group key, or both?
Remote attachments remain path text only in v1; is cross-instance file transfer required, or explicitly out of scope?
Inbound letters do not count against queen_mail.daily_limit; should they consume a separate per-peer quota?
When queen_mail.queens is omitted, all local queens are advertised; should an explicit list be required for safer defaults?
If the separate WAN design (docs/wan-peers-design.html) is adopted, should LAN and WAN share the ed25519 key/fingerprint storage, or keep separate identities?
